author: Omar Refaat
title: The caretakers
content:
Cairo – Summer 2025




Between the neck and the sword  




Yet, we go on, somehow, somewhen, somewhere. 




What’s making the unbearable bearable then? Who’s trying to make the fractured whole, the  paralysis somehow silently fruitful? Who’s trying to make the harshness of fate, hard not to adore and hard not to loathe fate, a feather more healthy? Who’s trying to reframe, to salvage, our maimed context on the run? 




Who, unsung, has been taking care of some of us in this beautiful brutal Cairo the past few, calamitous years? 




I looked around me and asked myself. 




What is love, in other words, and how is it being dispensed in the moonless waves of this incomprehensible grief?




What does love look like in the mutilated, public square now, mauled by this hellish, false reality shoved down our parched throats? What mermaid shapes is it taking in the fissures? In the plague of small, deranged men let loose on us, where does love drip, bloom calmly, lucidly, on its own? And we’re not even seeing it in the blur of our unfathomable resignation. Where do we, the afflicted of this earth, hold on, and who do we hold on to, hold dear, in this gale? What subtle kinds of repair are plugging the leak of meaning, the love-deficit, that won’t stop gushing with a grain of sand? Where is deliverance stealthily planting its seeds in abeyance, under the sign of this senseless dark

author: Mostafa Hosny
title: ‘Citizens’ health’ session at Egypt Forum 2026 boasts spending success with no mention of declining hospital bed numbers
content:
On Tuesday, the second day of Egypt Forum 2026, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar described the political leadership’s support for the healthcare sector as unprecedented.




Speaking at the “citizen’s health” 

session

 of Egypt Forum 2026, he said the approach dated back to the beginning of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s presidency in 2014, when, he 

said,

 Egypt faced a massive “disease burden,” with a lack of data and years of inadequate budget allocations that had failed to meet developmental ambitions for the system, particularly as population growth accelerated.




The minister said the state’s development plan had delivered gains in the sector, citing 16 presidential initiatives that had benefited 95 million citizens at a cost of LE44 billion. 




Abdel Ghaffar stressed that success in healthcare should not be measured by spending levels, but by the results citizens ultimately experience.




Mada Masr looked into some of those results, drawing from government 

data

 published by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).




One clear result over the time period is the notable decline in the number of beds in public hospitals between 2013 and 2024, with a drop from around 98,291 to 84,225. 




Over the same period, the number of beds in private hospitals rose from 26,009 to 36,014.

author: Mada Masr
title: Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah referred to trial on charges of running unlicensed website
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was referred to trial on Thursday on charges of establishing and managing a website without a license, according to lawyer Hassan al-Azhari, Mada Masr’s legal counsel.




The Supreme State Security Prosecution referred Attalah to trial at a New Cairo misdemeanors court, where sessions will begin on October 27.




The referral decision came after Attallah was questioned for over six hours by prosecutors on Wednesday at the Supreme State Security Prosecution headquarters in New Cairo. Prosecutors questioned her during the session on charges of running a website without a license and of publishing false news with the aim of disturbing public peace, with the latter accusation dropped from the charge sheet in the trial referral.




Azhari described the “haste” in the trial referral, which came just hours after the interrogation closed, and its scheduling for the coming week as “unjustified urgency” given the absence of circumstances in the case that require rapid resolution.




Wednesday’s investigation, labelled Supreme State Security Prosecution Case 9072/26, comprised information and documents compiled by the National Security Agency, including a report Mada Masr published earlier this month describing a 

wave of protests in prisons after the postponement of the criminal procedures law

, as well as a letter from the Supreme Media Regul

author: Mahmoud Bashir
title: Israeli forces arrest cancer patient, daughter returning to Gaza
content:
Israeli forces arrested two Palestinians on Tuesday evening as they were returning home to the Gaza Strip after traveling to Egypt for medical treatment, according to a statement from their family and one of their relatives who spoke to Mada Masr.




The two arrested, a cancer patient and her daughter, were among patients who were traveling both in and out of Gaza via the Rafah border crossing, which was reopened on Tuesday for the first time following its extended three-week closure by Occupation 

forces

.

 




Twenty-nine patients, along with 42 companions, 

left

 the Gaza Strip on Tuesday to receive treatment in Egyptian hospitals. Among them were critical cases, chronic disease patients and those with serious injuries. 

A group of 75 Palestinians returning to Gaza after receiving medical treatment abroad arrived via Rafah the same day to 

the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis.




The Rafah crossing, which was closed for almost two years after Israel 

occupied

 the crossing area in 2024, was 

reopened

 in February to provide passage to the sick and injured exiting Gaza for medical treatment, those returning from Egypt after completing treatment courses abroad, as well as for Palestinians who were 

stranded

 outside the strip and unable to return home amid Israel’s genocidal war.




Before they are allowed to return home, returnees must pass through exten

author: Mada Masr
title: Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah released by prosecutors on LE100,000 bail
content:
After investigations that lasted for over six hours, Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was ordered released by prosecutors on Wednesday evening on LE100,000 bail.




Attalah was questioned by the Supreme State Security Prosecution in Case 9072/2026 on charges of publishing false news inside and outside the country, with questions touching on a recently-published Mada Masr 

report

 concerning a wave of protest actions at a number of prisons across the country.




She was also questioned about Mada Masr’s work since its foundation, as well as about the steps its management has taken to obtain a license, according to lawyer Mokhtar Mounir.




Mada Masr has sought to obtain a license from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) on 

two

 

occasions

 since 2018.




On both occasions, it 

received

 no response. It was only informed of the SMRC’s rejection of the application in 2022, when Attalah was 

summoned

 for questioning in another case on charges of “running a website without the proper license.” She was presented with the rejection during that session.




Since then, Mada Masr has 

filed

 a lawsuit against the SMRC for damages incurred by its failure to inform the organization about its rejection of the application. The lawsuit was 

rejected

.

author: Mada Masr
title: Egypt Forum 2026 celebrates higher attendance at schools still struggling without teachers or classrooms
content:
Education has remained one of the main domestic fronts for the government in recent years, with chronic complaints around low spending in the sector.




At the start of the academic year in September, Education Minister Mohamed Abdel Latif faced fierce public and parliamentary pushback over controversial decisions affecting schools nationwide. 




Chief among them was the new enforcement of compulsory weekly assessments and homework, along with curriculum shakeups that drew formal parliamentary briefing requests accusing the ministry of running an evaluation regime that burns out students and teachers — who are already scarce — without improving learning.




Amid this simmering backlash, the Cabinet scrambled to stage-manage the narrative ahead of Egypt Forum 2026, a multi-day event mandated by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on October 1 to showcase national development and institutional dialogue.




After opening a window for people to register questions and concerns for discussion at the forum, the Cabinet said that education had outpaced all other issues with more than 15,000 public inquiries submitted on the topic, reflecting the degree of public concern.




We don’t know what these public inquiries were, as they have not been published in a publicly accessible location so far.




So, what did the government choose to talk about? 

In line with the presidency’s offici

author: Mada Masr
title: Youth and sports in rural areas: Greater access or declining participation?
content:
Increased state investment in youth and sports facilities was Sports Minister Gohar Nabil’s boast on the first day of the 

Egypt Forum 2026

, as part of the government’s tour of its own 

achievements

.




During a session titled “Youth and sports: From creating opportunities to making an impact,” Nabil 

pointed 

to more than LE31 billion spent on youth and sports facilities, including 4,382 youth centers, 23 sports stadiums, 40,000 youth center leagues, 12 youth and sports cities and 4,566 football pitches. He did not specify over what period those billions were spent.




Against the minister’s showpiece figures, the session made no mention of data from the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics, which show a sharp drop in the number of matches played and sports teams registered at village youth centers between 

2013

 and 

2024

, even as the number of centers went up.




According to CAPMAS’s 2013 and 2024 annual bulletins, the number of matches played by sports teams at village youth centers fell by 85.5 percent over the decade.




During the same period, the number of sports teams dropped by 50.3 percent, even though the number of centers rose by 6.7 percent.

author: Mada Masr
title: The future of rule: More questions than answers
content:
It took four days of successive presidential reiterations before the various parties began to grasp that, this time, it is different.




And no wonder. Never in Egypt’s modern history has the head of state chosen to hand power over voluntarily. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi himself 

promised

, time and again, during his first term that he would not move to amend the constitution and extend his rule. That changed at the start of his second term, when the constitution was in fact amended, and he secured two further terms, keeping him in office until 2030.




That’s why when the president opened his speech at the Armed Forces’ educational seminar on Wednesday by announcing he would not extend his rule, the confusion was plain on all sides, state institutions included.




At the seminar, Sisi said he had no intention of amending the Constitution. The audience hesitated for a few seconds before applauding. And many people 

noticed

.




The next day, he stated the announcement in clearer terms. But the statement, issued by the presidential spokesperson, was edited, changing “until 2030” into “until the last day of his rule.” There is a big difference between the two formulations. The latter preserves a measure of vagueness, which some apparently felt was needed until things became clearer.




Sisi alluded to this confusion on Saturday, at the Egyptian Military Academy’s fir

author: Mada Masr
title: State security prosecution summons Mada Masr editor-in-chief for investigation
content:
Lina Attalah, Mada Masr’s editor-in-chief, received a summons today from the Supreme State Security Prosecution to attend a questioning session on Wednesday, October 21. The summons did not say why she is being questioned.




The new investigation, Case 9072/2026, is the sixth case brought against Mada Masr, its journalists and its editor-in-chief in the past six years. The most recent was in August 2025, when the security prosecution released Attalah on LE30,000 bail. She was questioned at the time on charges of “broadcasting false news” and “using a website without a license,” based on a National Security Agency investigation report, in relation to a Mada Masr story on prisoners’ complaints of abuse in detention facilities. 

When 

asked 

why she trusted the sources cited in the story, Attalah said she had abided by professional journalistic standards and had acted in the public interest.

 She also pointed to the legally protected right to inform authorities of events through publication, noting that the outlet presents a full range of viewpoints.

The post 

State security prosecution summons Mada Masr editor-in-chief for investigation

 first appeared on 

Mada Masr

.

author: Lana Harb
title: Lebanon’s ‘pilot zone’ experiment: The case of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah
content:
Ihsan Yaghi’s house in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah is scorched from the inside. Piles of rubble fill the rooms she and her husband walk through to see what remains. What was not demolished by nearby Israeli strikes has been blackened by fire, with soot covering the interior walls. But Yaghi refuses to leave.




“Despite everything, this is still my land, and we have a very strong attachment to this land that we can’t let go of,” Yaghi tells Mada Masr.




Yaghi’s is one of roughly 100 families that have, since July, returned to Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, one of around 70 villages in southern Lebanon still under Israeli occupation, its residents displaced, its homes destroyed, its fields unreachable. The question of what should be done for the south, how to rebuild and how to return people to their land under continued occupation, has become one of the most pressing political questions in Lebanon. The answer currently on offer from the Lebanese government and its international partners is the “pilot zone.”




On July 21, the United States announced 

the official commencement

 of pilot zone operations in three villages in southern Lebanon: Froun, Srifa and Zawtar al-Gharbiyah. The model emerged from the framework agreement — a US-mediated trilateral framework signed by Lebanon and Israel on June 26, under which the Lebanese military is to restore sovereign authority over all Lebanese terri

author: Mada Masr
title: Parliament puts off vote on authorizing Sisi to send troops to Saudi Arabia until Tuesday
content:
After a closed session on Sunday that ran for nearly three hours, the House of Representatives postponed a vote on authorizing President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi to send troops on a combat mission to defend Saudi Arabia, putting it off until after Monday’s and Tuesday’s sessions.




Sisi had called for an emergency parliamentary session during the Egyptian Military Academy graduation ceremony on Saturday, asking lawmakers to authorize him to take any measures necessary to protect Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks “if we are asked to do so.”




The delay came after MPs demanded details of the Armed Forces’ role in Saudi Arabia beyond the National Defense Council’s 

statement

, asking that every MP get a chance to express their views on the matter, according to three lawmakers who spoke to Mada Masr.




MP Ehab Mansour, the Egyptian Social Democratic Party parliamentary bloc head, told Mada Masr after the session that members were instructed not to share details of the discussions with the media.




“We are not looking for a role to play, but it makes no sense whatsoever for us to allow any harm to come to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, its security or its stability,” Sisi said during the graduation ceremony.




He appealed to “everyone in the Gulf” to stop the war. “Regardless of this appeal, whether it is heeded or not, Egypt, in line with His Majesty King Salman and Crown P

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: Govt scrambles to solve fuel crisis without clear end in sight, divided on fava bean import ban; Quintet tries to balance competing political initiatives; RSF continues Blue Nile push; Military sets sights on Darfur
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

 here

.




The struggling wartime economy took center stage this week in Sudan with a pair of issues at the heart of daily life.




The first is a fuel crisis that has grown increasingly worse in recent weeks as gas stations have become makeshift campsites and prices have skyrocketed. While the government has projected an outward image of assurance, behind closed doors, the wheels are turning to try to bring fuel to the nine states under military control.




The plan has two axes, sources informed of the discussion told Mada Masr. The first is essentially a triage: tighten fuel allocations and movement to where it is needed. Various government bodies have tried their hand at centralizing authority to better streamline decision-making, but Sudan’s fractured executive apparatus has seen more attempts than results.




The second part of the plan would require solving the issue at its source: bringing in new supplies to offset the non-performing domestic oil sector. For this, Transitional Sovereignty Council chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan is holding talks with Saudi Arabia. But as an informed TSF source told Mada Masr, the government cannot commit to a timeline to end the crisis until external agreements are finalized and the necessary financial guarantees are in place.




Alongside the fuel crisis, more potential trouble looms on the

author: Mada Masr
title: As Sisi vows to leave power by 2030, sources differ on whether he really means it
content:
Speaking at the 44th Cultural and Educational Symposium of the Egyptian Armed Forces on 

Wednesday

, President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi 

said

 Egypt’s “Constitution would not be touched.”

 




His remarks came as part of a longer speech warning against a return to the demonstrations and protests that swept the country after 2011, alongside a series of other political messages, including a 

declaration

 that he 

would

 “never tire of protecting Egypt.”

 

He reiterated similar messages again on 

Thursday,

 during a speech at the Police Academy’s graduation ceremony, saying he would continue working “until the final day” of his presidential term in 2030.




With 

talk

 of lifting presidential term limits already a feature of political conversations in the leadup to the 2025 parliamentary election, a parliamentary source told Mada Masr at the time, Sisi’s comments sparked immediate queries about how long the president will remain in power.

 




Speaking on condition of anonymity, three parliamentary sources close to a sovereign security agency told Mada Masr that Sisi’s pledge not to touch the Constitution is inseparable from a broader plan to reshape the country’s political landscape, and is driven by his desire to avoid the mistakes of ousted President Hosny Mubarak, whose three decades in power fostered the widespread resentment that would lead to the 2011 revolut

author: Nadia Salem
title: ‘Revolution, the dirty word’: On Lara Baladi’s Z for Zarafa
content:
What happens after revolution? How do we remember, if we do at all?




In her exhibition, Z for Zarafa, which opened at Gypsum Gallery at the start of June and closed on September 23, Lara Baladi takes us through a scavenger hunt of moments, leading us into an archive of revolution, specifically looked at from an aftermath vantage point of movement, migration, displacement and the ultimate wrestling for freedom.




The exhibition acts as a physical installation of aspects of an online database, 

Anatomy of Revolution

, which is a project exploring the various iconography and language of resistance movements. The database 

consolidates

 research, visual, written and audio material from past and present global struggles, which Baladi gathered between 2011 and 2021 as part of her project, 

Vox Populi, Tahrir Archives

. The body of data, a vast space of references, is organized into an abecedary using the Arabic alphabet, designed to work as “an educational primer of struggles for freedom.”




The exhibition, a multi-year effort through a wide network of collaborations, brought together the works of editors, writers and visual artists reflecting on experiences of migration and exile, alongside the works of refugee women in Cairo, blacksmiths in Imbaba, antiquaries in downtown Cairo, embroiderers in Islamic Cairo and potters in Fayoum, among others.

author: Shams Eddin Essam
title: Will Supply Ministry’s wheat intervention really rein in cost of unsubsidized bread?
content:
As the grain and bakery industries petition the government for permission to increase bread prices in order to protect their profits, the Supply Ministry has 

announced

 it is injecting wheat onto the national commodity exchange to bring prices down and cut production costs.




The move came after calls for a government review of bread pricing guidelines in 

August

 and 

September

. Producers said they needed to increase consumer prices to compensate for rising production costs, particularly of flour. 

Despite talks between ministry and industry representatives, the government has held the price caps and loaf weight specifications 

steady

, announcing the supply release instead.




However, sources from the grain, milling and bakery industries who spoke to Mada Masr expressed doubt that the mechanism would meaningfully reduce production costs, indicating that the last time the ministry undertook a similar supply allocation in 2023, the move only fuelled profiteering on a secondary market that emerged in parallel to the commodity exchange.




The ministry has not said how much wheat it will offer via the commodity exchange, though ministry spokespeople 

explained

 that the extra supply would be enough to bring costs down across the supply chain.

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Ehsan Salah
title: Sudan, Egypt to pursue joint border security, as public tensions flare after deadly mine bombing
content:
In the aftermath of the bombing of a mine in the 

Halayeb Triangle

 that left scores of Sudanese miners dead, Egypt and Sudan are discussing a new security framework along the countries’ shared eastern border.

 




That framework would provide for joint coordination to pursue what both sides regard as security risks arising from organized crime, Sudanese and Egyptian officials 

told

 Mada Masr.




The push toward closer coordination comes amid public outcry in Sudan and diplomatic concern in international quarters over the killing of scores of artisanal miners in the disputed 

Halayeb Triangle

 on Saturday.

 




That public outcry was accentuated on Monday when a gunman killed two Egyptians in a main market in southern Khartoum in what Sudanese security officials involved in the investigations told Mada Masr was a retaliatory attack.




The shooting took place at around 2 pm near the 

Export Development Bank in the Local Market

, a security source in 

Khartoum State police

 told Mada Masr.

 Three Egyptians were targeted in the market’s commercial area. 

Two died at the scene, while the third was taken to the 

Omdurman Medical Corps Hospital 

for treatment.




Ali al-Laouta, a vegetable seller at the market, witnessed Monday’s shooting. 

He told Mada Masr that he noticed a man wearing a 

military uniform bearing the badge of the joint force of military-all

author: Mada Masr
title: Protests at several prisons, detainee ‘banishments’ surround delay to Criminal Procedure Code
content:
A wave of protests has swept through several prisons over the last three weeks, as prisoners who were hopeful that the new Criminal Procedure Code would bring an end to their prolonged remand detention had their hopes dashed at the eleventh hour when the law’s implementation was postponed, according to several lawyers acting in defense of detainees held at different prisons who spoke separately to Mada Masr over the same time period.




The postponement pushed back what many detainees saw as a window of opportunity for authorities to release dozens of them held in remand after the law’s awaited implementation on October 1.




With that window now firmly shut until October 2027, a wave of demonstrations in detention centers has been met by security forces with measures that the lawyers say include the punitive transfer of detainees to prisons farther away from their families, a practice known as “

taghreeb”

 (banishment).




As cries and claims about the demonstrations and the security forces’ response made their way to social media, the Interior Ministry issued repeated denials that protests and abuses are taking place within prisons, most recently in an October 2 

statement

. The Public Prosecution, meanwhile, was yet to issue a statement regarding the claims at the time of publishing.

author: Mada Masr
title: State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days
content:
The detention of six journalists from fact-checking platform Matsda2sh was renewed for 15 days on Tuesday evening, pending further investigations, according to their lawyers. The renewal was ordered by the Supreme State Security Prosecution during today’s hearing in Case 8083/2026.




The journalists Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira, Abdallah Kadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal are being investigated in the case, registered with the Supreme State Security Prosecution, and were questioned again by prosecutors in sessions on Tuesday.




The journalists’ lawyers told Mada Masr that questioning began around 1 pm and continued into the evening at the prosecution’s headquarters in the Fifth Settlement. The sessions revisited previous lines of questioning, including questioning about wages, the managerial structure of the platform and the way work was organized, with no new evidence presented to the journalists.




All six journalists have been held at Badr 1 Prison since they were brought before the prosecution early last week. Their lawyers said they are due to receive their first family visits starting Thursday, as well as to be granted dedicated time for exercise.




Security forces arrested the six Matsda2sh journalists in the span of24 hours 

during a campaign 

launched on September 28 which targeted the fact-checking platform’s team across several

author: Roaa Reda
title: From journalists’ pursuit to protection? Bid to ban jail sentences for publishing gets boost from syndicate, MPs
content:
Parliamentarians, legal advocates and representatives of the Journalists Syndicate gathered on Saturday at the Cairo syndicate headquarters for an open seminar to discuss practical steps to curb the use of detention against journalists in lawsuits related to the act of publishing.




Participants noted that, despite an explicit constitutional protection against the practice, there is a lack of mechanisms to support a change — a situation which prompted the drafting, almost a decade ago, of a law to prevent imprisonment in publishing crimes.




In an attempt to activate the dormant draft law, Tagammu Party MP Atef Maghawry told Mada Masr that he began on Monday to gather lawmakers’ support for the bill, telling Mada Masr he will seek to complete the effort over the coming weeks to secure the bill’s presentation in Parliament’s general session.




The discussion came on the back of the ongoing detention of six journalists from independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh, whose arrests earlier this month brought the number of journalists detained in relation to their work to 26.




Multiple voices at the seminar highlighted the risks facing both journalists and citizens alike given the expansion of legal grounds for the arrest of journalists over recent years.




Among the attendees was the father of cartoonist and translator Ashraf Omar, who spoke of his son’s imprisonment

author: Mada Masr
title: Scores killed, Sudan announces an investigation, Egypt a new phase of anti-illegal gold mining campaign
content:
In the first official comment since a mine near the Sudanese-Egyptian border was bombed on Saturday killing scores of miners, Sudan’s Transitional Sovereignty Council 

issued

 a statement on Monday to mourn the souls of “Sudanese citizens who lost their lives in the painful incident involving a number of Sudanese miners in the border area between Sudan and the Arab Republic of Egypt.”

 




Without providing further details on when, how or where the Sudanese nationals died, the executive authority that has ruled Sudan since 2019 announced that a fact-finding committee composed of members of the Sudanese Public Prosecution as well as relevant judicial and security authorities would be formed to investigate the matter. 




The council underlined that “leadership in both brotherly countries,” referring to Egypt, have “remained in continuous communication immediately after the incident occurred, ensuring the protection of lives, preserving the relationship between the two brotherly peoples, understanding the details of the incident and sharing the facts with public opinion.” 




Later on Monday evening, the Egyptian Armed Forces spokesperson released a statement announcing the implementation of the “third phase of the large-scale campaign to confront illegal gold mining in the Eastern Desert, after dropping warning leaflets on criminal elements to impose full sovereignty withi

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: RSF preps new front from Ethiopia, pummels Blue Nile; In Kordofan, RSF conducts ‘field’ executions, digs in heels at Nuhud; Dagris prison dispute stalls registry; Gov’t criticizes UN fact-finding renewal
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

 

here

.




With all eyes turned toward the escalating conflict in Ethiopia that is teetering on the brink of becoming a wider regional war, the Rapid Support Forces stepped up their attacks on the Sudan war’s southeastern front this week. 




Blue Nile’s 

Wad al-Mahi

 locality in the east of the state bore the brunt of the escalation. The RSF launched an attack from Ethiopia on Saturday and seized the Kadalo mountains area, which sits near the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and Roseires Dam reservoir. This coincided with a drone campaign against Damazin, which included strikes on the homes of Blue Nile Governor Ahmed Badry and Regional Finance Minister Abbas Kara, fuel stations, military sites, universities and mosques. 




The military has hit back, launching airstrikes on RSF positions in 

Wad al-Mahi and tried to reassure residents. As of Sunday, about 

2,800 people are estimated to have been displaced from 10 villages in Wad al-Mahi.




But action in the southeastern front wasn’t limited to the Blue Nile. Large numbers of RSF fighters have been moved from Darfur to Addis Ababa in recent weeks in preparation to transfer them toward Sudan’s eastern border, where they are expected to gear up for an attack on the Fashaga border strip in Gadarif State, according to an RSF source and another source informed of the mobilizatio

author: Mada Masr
title: Prosecution says journalists’ testimony indicates Matsda2sh was ‘Brotherhood media cell,’ EIPR says statement unproven position
content:
The Public Prosecution issued a 

statement

 on Wednesday regarding the investigations into the six Matsda2sh fact-checking platform’s journalists, stating that one of them admitted that all the defendants — as well as others — had joined a media committee affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood.

 




It said they had been tasked with carrying out “media plans” based on spreading and broadcasting rumors and false news about state institutions, exclusively highlighting the shortcomings of those institutions, disparaging the roles and performance of their officials and overblowing issues related to select groups, as well as fabricating and exaggerating events related to them. 




From its side, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists, repeated its demands for their release, for the charges against them to be dropped and for the case to be closed.




In 

response

 to the prosecution’s statement, EIPR said that its media statements published on social media hold no evidentiary value in law and amount only to a summary of the prosecution’s case, none of which has been presented before a court, while none of its claims has been proven.

 




The organization pointed out the prosecution’s failure to address the fact that the six journalists did not appear before the prosecution until five days after

author: Hassan Alnaser
title: How the Dagalos’ ever tightening hold on power destabilized the RSF project
content:
Daein. Amid the rain showers veiling the city in the first week of August, the fourth August of the war, four-wheel-drive vehicles pull up one after another. Out of them come men who know the villages and firgan that have sent fighters into the Rapid Support Forces, who know the families who have been giving up their sons to war since April 2023.




Abdel Rahim Dagalo sits opposite the Rizeigat tribal omdas who have come from across Darfur’s different localities. Trees ring the meeting place, shielding it from the eyes of drones. He wants one thing from them: to mobilize again.




The tribal leaders begin by talking about the soldiers wounded in battle, about fighters who came home missing limbs, a source who attended the meeting tells Mada Masr. They speak of families who lost their sons, of men who went to the front and never came back, and of communities that, for more than three years, have borne the cost of a war whose military and political decisions they have no hand in.




Then the conversation turns to the men the leadership still wants to send to fight. The omdas say they can no longer persuade their tribes to mobilize as they did in the first years of the war. The war has dragged on, and the losses have piled up. People have begun asking about the sons they sent to the front, about treatment for the wounded, asking what place these communities that gave up their m

author: Mada Masr
title: Officials approve island residents’ demand to remain, Staying on Warraq movement says
content:
State officials have agreed to provide Warraq Island’s residents with alternative housing under a “house-for-a-house” scheme, which was one of the residents’ main demands, to allow them to remain on the land as the state advances its development plan, the Staying on Warraq 

movement

 

announced

 on Tuesday. 




The plan is yet to be announced by any agency representing the government, however.




The movement formed in August has led negotiations with state authorities following the latest round of 

clashes

 between residents and security forces. A security deployment is regularly stationed at the Nile island’s ferry and transit points to secure supply lines and construction at the state-led redevelopment project, which has for years threatened to force residents from their homes and restricted their access to goods and essential services.




The new agreement was established in a Saturday meeting between several of the island’s representatives, both members and non-members of the movement, and state officials.




Officials told the movement that residents’ demand for a “house-for-a-house” guarantee had been approved and was now a reality, with an official decision expected to be issued and announced “within a short period,” according to the movement’s statement.

author: Mada Masr
title: Syndicate submits prosecution complaint regarding Matsda2sh journalists’ torture, Interior Ministry denies claims
content:
Prosecutors are still investigating the six Matsda2sh journalists who are being held in remand detention for 15 days, effective from the day they were brought before the Supreme State Security Prosecution, according to Hossam Bahgat, the director of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists. 




Prosecutors largely repeated the same line of questioning the journalists faced in the first round of interrogations, focusing on the platform’s editorial policy and their professional backgrounds, according to lawyers informed of the investigations.




 Journalists from the independent fact-checking platform had previously been held at National Security Agency premises for almost an entire week, following the arrest campaign that targeted six of the outlet’s team members. 




After several of the journalists described being forced to record false “confessions” on camera and being subjected to torture at the hands of the National Security Agency officers, the Journalists Syndicate published a 

statement

 on Monday night saying its members had decided “unanimously” to file a complaint with the public prosecutor regarding the charges.

 




Although prosecutors had decided that one of the journalists should be sent for a forensic medical examination to document signs of torture, he is yet to be brought in

author: Moataz Hagag
title: State security prosecution releases journalist Rasha Azab on LE10,000 bail
content:
Journalist Rasha Azab was released on LE10,000 bail on Monday evening by the Supreme State Security Prosecution following questioning in relation to a tweet she published in recent weeks regarding the conduct of the Interior Ministry and its impact on the public mood. 




She was questioned on charges of “promoting the perpetration of terrorist acts” and using a website to promote ideas calling for doing so in Supreme State Security Prosecution Case 8025/2026, her defense lawyer, Ragia Omran, told Mada Masr. 




Azab was questioned on her reasons for publishing a tweet, in which she wrote, on September 23, “how long does it take to go from ‘the Interior Ministry are thugs’ to ‘the people want the fall of the regime.’” Azab responded that her tweet was commentary on the case of Dina Ezzat, a woman who called for her husband’s release on social media in September, after he was arrested from their Nasr City home by authorities in their local area. Ezzat herself was briefly 

taken

 into custody after she spoke out against her husband’s arrest before she was later released on bail. 




According to the case’s record, 12 people filed complaints at police stations across several governorates against Azab the day after she posted her tweet, Omran said.




The prosecution did not question her about the Matsda2sh case. Azab herself, however, pointed to what she had read on social m

author: Mada Masr
title: Matsda2sh journalists forced to read false ‘confessions’ statements to camera, subjected to torture in custody
content:
Several of the Matsda2sh journalists arrested last week were forced to record false “confessions” and subjected to torture and ill-treatment while being held at National Security Agency premises, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), whose lawyers are representing the six journalists, 

stated

 on Monday morning.




EIPR lawyers attended investigation sessions with five of the independent fact-checking platform’s journalists on Sunday evening, when they were presented before prosecuting authorities for the first time since the start of the security campaign that saw six of Matsda2sh’s journalists arrested and forcibly disappeared within the span of 24 hours between September 28 and 29.




The Supreme State Security Prosecution interrogated Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira for over 10 hours beginning on Saturday evening and issued orders he be 

held

 in remand for 15 days pending further investigations.




The other five journalists were presented before prosecutors on Sunday evening and were each questioned for over 10 hours over the course of the night.




Lawyers were present with them during the investigation sessions, but the detainees were not allowed to consult with them privately. The prosecution is yet to issue detention orders for Abdallah Qadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal.

author: Mada Masr
title: Security prosecution detains Abu Emaira for 15 days, whereabouts of 5 other Matsda2sh journalists unknown
content:
Journalist Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira has been issued a 15-day detention order by the Supreme State Security Prosecution, Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights lawyer Islam Salama told Mada Masr.




Abu Emaira was presented before prosecutors for the first time at 10 pm on Saturday night, five days after security authorities launched an arrest campaign targeting him and five of his colleagues from the independent fact-checking platform, Matsda2sh.




The whereabouts of the other five Matsda2sh journalists are still unknown as of time of publishing.




Salama told Mada Masr he attended with Abu Emaira the investigation session which began at 10 pm on Saturday evening and continued for over 10 hours. Prosecutors questioned Abu Emaira during the session on three criminal charges: joining a terrorist group, publishing and broadcasting false news, and using a social media platform to these ends.




The investigation was established as Supreme State Security Case 8083/2026.




Prosecutors questioned Abu Emaria about several items published on Matsda2sh’s platform. They asked how topics are selected for coverage and questioned him regarding the purpose and aim of publication, EIPR head Hossam Bahgat told Mada Masr.




Before his arrival at the prosecution premises, Abu Emaira had been held at National Security Agency premises for the five preceding days, his lawyer learned duri

author: Mada Masr
title: Dozens join syndicate demonstration to call for Matsda2sh journalists’ release
content:
Dozens of journalists participated on Saturday in a symbolic sit-in inside the Journalists Syndicate to call for the release of the Matsda2sh journalists, whose whereabouts remain unknown after security forces launched an arrest campaign targeting six of the independent fact-checking platform’s staff on Monday.




While the sit-in was scheduled to end at 5 pm, several members of the syndicate’s general assembly announced that they would remain inside the syndicate, keeping the sit-in open-ended until the Matsda2sh journalists are released.




The syndicate’s board also announced that an emergency meeting would be convened on Monday with a single clause on the agenda: how to respond to the arrest of the six journalists.




Syndicate head Khaled al-Balshy told attendees that the Supreme State Security Prosecution informed the syndicate’s lawyer that the detained journalists have not yet been investigated by the prosecution.




This was confirmed to 

Mada Masr

 on Saturday by the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ head, Hossam Bahgat, who said that the prosecution head had denied a 

report

 published by the privately owned Al-Masry Al-Youm claiming that the prosecution had issued a decision to detain the journalists for 15 days.




In its 

statement

, Matsda2sh called upon journalists to take action in the wake of the campaign against them, describing the arrest c

author: Mada Masr
title: Unconfirmed report asserts official detention order issued for Matsda2sh team amid security leaks, media accusations
content:
A report that emerged on Friday night has claimed that the Supreme State Security Prosecution issued a formal detention order on Thursday for the six journalists from the Matsda2sh editorial team who were arrested earlier in the week.  




The Al-Masry Al-Youm report described the issuance as ordering the journalists’ detention for 15 days.




But as no official announcement has been published by prosecuting authorities, lawyers and a Journalists Syndicate source speaking to Mada Masr cast doubt on the veracity of the news report’s claim, which represents the first indication of an official detention order since the journalists’ arrests. 




Security forces arrested and forcibly disappeared the six members of the Matsda2sh editorial team in the span of 24 hours in a campaign that was launched Monday night. No official statement on the arrest was published until Thursday.




None of the journalists have been presented formally before prosecuting authorities, EIPR lawyers told Mada Masr, and neither their families nor the Journalists Syndicate have been informed of their place of detention, the syndicate source confirmed. 




The Al-Masry Al-Youm 

report

 was back-dated to October 1, but was not available to readers until late on October 2.

 The report stated that a 15-day detention order had been issued for the six journalists following the Interior Ministry’s Thursday a

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: Ethiopia accuses Sudan of backing opposition, reshuffled hope for Idris’s govt, tribal violence engulfs South Darfur, military opens road to West Kordofan, China on Sudan’s coast
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

 

here

.




Sudan’s government is taking a long hard look in the mirror, and they don’t like what they see, sources close to Prime Minister Kamel Idris and the Transitional Sovereignty Council 

told

 Mada Masr this week.

 




Ushered in on a promise of hope a year ago, Idris’s government has faced significant issues. Some of those come down to war-time trials, but infighting and attempts to delimit the remit of a civilian government backed by a powerful and intrusive military council have been persistent issues. 




Now the government is considering a reshuffle of ministerial and gubernatorial appointments to address executive imbalances and shortfalls, particularly on economic and service-related issues, according to a source in Idris’s office.




While Idris and the TSC may see an administrative reshuffle as a way to address war-time woes, the armed movements that signed the 2020 Juba peace agreement insist that any bureaucratic rearrangement must not change the power-sharing agreement inked in the South Sudanese capital. 




For now, the reshuffle is all just talk. But the movements do not view it in isolation from the larger reshaping of the political landscape of recent months, a leader in one of the Juba armed movements told Mada Masr, particularly as the planned national dialogue will have to address their relationship

author: Rana Mamdouh
title: Prisoner protests, lack of readiness delay enactment of new Criminal Procedures Law
content:
The Criminal Procedures Code’s deferred enactment, 

approved

 by Parliament yesterday, was attributed by MPs and the government to a lack of preparedness.

 However, parliamentary and legal sources told Mada Masr the impact of the law’s enactment on the hundreds of detainees being held in remand could be among the reasons that led to the last-minute postponement. 




The bill to postpone the law’s enactment, brought forth by the Nation’s Future Party, which is close to state authorities, proposed an amendment to the 2025 bill to delay enforcement until October 2027, replacing an article in the original text that had set October 1 as the operative date.




According to Parliament, the decision to enforce the new bill next year was taken primarily out of concern for the readiness of the digital system, which the law stipulates be used for judicial notifications and remote court proceedings.




During yesterday’s Legislative Committee meeting ahead of the plenary session vote on the postponement draft, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Hany Hanna 

said

 the ministry backed the bill in order to allow for greater preparedness ahead of implementation, noting that “some courts have been prepared, while others, such as felony appeal courts, still need preparation.”




But the Justice Ministry had issued several decisions in August which indicated its readiness to implement the dig

author: Faisal Ali, Hassan Alnaser, Hazem Tharwat, Kidus Lemma
title: How a war in Tigray could set off a more complex fight
content:
For much of the past year, tensions between Ethiopia’s federal government and authorities in the northern Tigray region had been steadily escalating toward confrontation.




The threat for those in Tigray, as much as for those in the wider region, was that the area could tip back into the kind of war that devastated the state between 2020 and 2022, but, this time, with a supercharged regional dimension. Officials in Addis Ababa and Mekelle, Tigray’s capital, have traded increasingly hostile accusations as the peace established at Pretoria frayed, while intermittent clashes and drone strikes produced episodes of serious violence. 




From the sidelines, Eritrea, Egypt, Somalia and Sudan — a pragmatic, loosely aligned anti-Ethiopia coalition — looked on. Then, on September 20, a drone struck a truck carrying more than 41 tons of food aid for displaced people in northwestern Tigray, setting the vehicle and its cargo ablaze.




Aftermath of a drone strike on a humanitarian aid truck in northwestern Tigray, September 22. Courtesy: @JoeTseGy on X




Three days later, Tigrayan forces seized three airports across the region. Fighting then spread beyond Tigray into neighboring Afar and Amhara. The federal government accused the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) of launching an offensive, while Tigrayan authorities said their forces were responding to federal attacks involving

author: Nadia Salem
title: Interior Ministry accuses Matsda2sh of belonging to Muslim Brotherhood in claim founder says ‘authorities know is untrue’
content:
Over 48 hours since authorities initiated the arrest and forced disappearance of six Matsda2sh journalists, the Interior Ministry acknowledged on Thursday morning that it had detained the independent fact-checking platform’s staff. 




The journalists’ whereabouts remain unknown, according to their legal representatives at the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, and they have not been presented for investigation before prosecuting authorities.




The ministry accused the journalists of belonging to the Muslim Brotherhood, a claim the founder of the independent fact-checking platform said authorities know to be untrue in comments to Mada Masr.




In the statement published Thursday morning, the Interior Ministry 

said

 Matsda2sh aims to undermine the country’s stability by “fabricating lies and spreading rumors.” The statement added that it is an unlicensed page, managed from abroad to broadcast false news and distort facts. It also accused the platform’s founder, Abdel Rahman Mansour, of being a “fugitive member of the Brotherhood” and that he is working in cooperation with “a number of  Brotherhood elements in other countries, in exchange for funding they receive from abroad.”




EIPR lawyer Islam Salama said that the six journalists have still not been brought before the Supreme State Security Prosecution, which handles terrorism investigations, and said authoritie

author: Hassan Alnaser
title: Drones target Addis Ababa military headquarters; Federal forces advance on Tigrayan capital
content:
The Ethiopian military headquarters in Addis Ababa was targeted in a drone attack in the early hours of Thursday, an Ethiopian security source in the capital told Mada Masr. 




At 6 am, Ethiopian defense systems detected a “simultaneous terrorist attack attempt using suicide drones targeting vital facilities within the capital,” the security source said. “The attack aimed to strike the military command headquarters in the Tor Hailoch area, as well as the vicinity of the 24th Infantry Division headquarters in the Kirkos district of central Addis Ababa.”




A resident of Tor Hailoch who lives near the Ethiopian military headquarters reported hearing  two explosions near the headquarters, the first at 6:30 am and another 45 minutes later. 




The resident told Mada Masr that he saw ambulances and fire trucks rushing through the streets shortly after the blast.




The security source suggested that the drones were downed by the Ethiopian National Defense Force’s air defense systems. 




“Our technical and engineering teams are currently conducting a precise and comprehensive assessment of the material damage caused by projectile shrapnel and are tracing the launch points of these drones, while security forces have established a tight security perimeter and are on high alert around the targeted sites to ensure operational safety.”




The attack comes hours after the Ethiopian

author: Mada Masr
title: Parliament approves last-minute delay to Criminal Procedures Code enactment
content:
The Criminal Procedures Code’s enactment was 

postponed

 for one year, after Parliament gave their final approval to an amendment during an emergency session on Wednesday morning.




The law, which has been 

likened

 to “a second constitution” in terms of its foundational importance to Egypt’s legal system, was due to come into effect less than 24 hours after the session, on October 1.




Parliamentary Affairs Minister Hany Hanna 

attended

 the session to argue in favor of the postponement, which he said had been called for by over 60 MPs — the required quorum for a proposal’s presentation to the plenary session.




Hanna, whose comments were relayed in a Cabinet 

statement

 on Wednesday evening, expressed the government’s backing for the postponement, adding that it would ensure the law’s provisions can be implemented without obstacles. He specifically highlighted the benefit this extra time would grant in allowing for the completion of the new digital system — to be used for judicial notifications and remote court proceedings — while also ensuring that it can be properly tested.

author: Mada Masr
title: Six Matsda2sh journalists arrested, forcibly disappeared
content:
Six Matsda2sh journalists have been arrested in a security campaign that began on Monday night with raids on the journalists’ homes, according to 

Matsda2sh

 and the 

Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights

, whose lawyers represent the reporters.

 




The whereabouts of Matsda2sh staff Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira, Abdallah Qadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal remain unknown. No one has been allowed to contact their families or legal team, EIPR stated Tuesday morning. 




“The reasons for their arrest remain unknown. It is also unclear which authority is investigating them, and there is still no confirmed information regarding where they are being held,” said Matsda2sh in a statement announcing the first arrests on Tuesday evening.




The Journalists Syndicate released a statement on Tuesday 

night

 demanding the Matsda2sh journalists are immediately and unconditionally released, stating that the syndicate’s legal department would take immediate action.




A syndicate source told Mada Masr that family members had described ill-treatment during the arrests to the syndicate.




The move to arrest an entire newsroom is a significant crackdown.




“I believe this is the first time in the two-century history of Egyptian journalism that an entire newsroom, with all its journalists, has been arrested after their homes were raided,” 

sa

author: Moataz Hagag, Mada Masr
title: Italian court sentences 3 Egyptian officers to jail in Regeni murder case
content:
An Italian court 

sentenced

 on Monday three Egyptian security officers to 10 years imprisonment in absentia for the 2016 kidnapping of Giulio Regeni.

 




The convicted officers are Major Magdy Sherif of the National Security Agency and police officers Colonel Ather Kamal and Colonel Hesham Helmy. 




The court dismissed the charge of 

conspiracy to commit aggravated murder

 that was leveled against Sherif, while another security official implicated in the case, 

Major General Tarek Saber, was acquitted of all charges.

 




The Italian prosecution had requested in its closing arguments a life sentence for Sherif and 17 years and six months for the three other defendants.




“A ruling issued in the name of the Italian people, a ruling that stands as a safeguard for all the Giulios and Giulias of the world,” said Alessandra Ballerini, the family’s lawyer. Ballerini added that the verdict proves that the body of evidence presented before the court withstood its scrutiny.




“From this evening on, all regimes, along with their apparatuses and agents, will be forced to remember that human dignity is inviolable, as are human bodies; that impunity can be defeated; and that democracies can put a stop to arbitrary abuse,” she added.




Riccardo Noury, Amnesty International Italy’s spokesperson, believes the verdict played an important role in “scratching the wall of impuni

author: Shams Eddin Essam
title: Supply Ministry postpones bread price review amid ongoing push from bakeries, mills
content:
Supply Minister Sherif Farouk has asked for a week’s review period before the ministry responds to a request to raise its guideline consumer prices for two categories of non-subsidized bread, according to a source who was present at a Sunday 

meeting

 where representatives from bakeries and mills put forward their request.




The request is their second in just a few months, following a dispute over the extent of the ministry’s role in setting and enforcing non-subsidized bread prices.




Their push for higher guideline prices comes as the industry’s production costs rise steadily, with wheat prices spiralling again amid an escalation in the intensity of Russia’s war on Ukraine, and as domestic fuel prices continue to rise against the backdrop of the regional war.




Farouk said the ministry would review price movements over the coming week, and, if prices did not fall over that period, the ministry would revise guideline prices for the tourist and fino bread categories, the source said. The ministry did not commit to a specific percentage increase.




Senior representatives of the General Bakeries Division raised the issue of production costs at the meeting and called for a review of tourist and fino bread prices, proposing a 15 percent increase.




Milling sector representatives also presented an update on the wheat and flour markets and recent pressures on production

author: Sara Seif Eddin
title: Govt tells BP it would block sale of company’s Egypt assets to Energean
content:
The government informed British Petroleum it would reject a deal that would see the British company sell some of its Egypt based oil and gas assets to Israeli majority-owned Energean, according to two sources informed of the deal who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, one of whom who works for the company. 




The stance was communicated during a meeting in Cairo on Thursday between Petroleum Minister Karim Badawy and BP Executive Vice President Gordon Birrell, they said.




One reason the government gave for rejecting the potential deal was “national security imperatives,” according to the BP source. Other concerns relate to the wide gap in technical capabilities between the two companies, particularly in deep water drilling, an area where Energean’s capacity is comparatively limited, the source said.




The meeting came as BP seeks to divest part of its energy asset portfolio in Egypt, while the government is pushing to attract more investment into the petroleum sector in order to raise natural gas production amid a major energy shortfall.




Media reports have pointed to exclusive talks between BP and Energean over the latter’s purchase of some of BP’s assets in Egypt, although no deal has been officially announced.




Any change in ownership of oil fields between producing companies requires the approval of the government, represented by the Egyptian General

author: Mada Masr
title: With region in turmoil Madbuly, Abdel Atty go to UNGA
content:
As diplomats and heads of states from around the world descend on New York this week to hold official and unofficial talks during the United Nations General Assembly, the already-long ledger of regional crises continues to grow.




In recent weeks the Houthis have taken key areas overlooking the crucial Bab al-Mandab Strait, triggering renewed fighting in Yemen. Meanwhile in Ethiopia, the long-simmering tensions in Tigray have boiled over, with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front 

seizing

 on Wednesday the restive northern state’s three airports and setting the stage for what could become another complex regional war in the Horn of Africa.




This is in addition to the continued war in Sudan, the threat of escalation in Iran, the dire oil crisis that the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz has created, and the stalled diplomatic process on Gaza.




Egypt finds itself at the intersection, if not directly involved in many of these crises. To represent Egypt’s position at the mega-diplomatic forum that is the UNGA, President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly for the second year in a row to lead Cairo’s delegation.




Sisi led Egypt’s delegations to the UNGA himself from 2014 to 2019. Since then, he has sent his foreign minister in his place: first Sameh Shoukry, who held the post from 2014 to 2024, and now Badr Abdel Atty.

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: Rizeigat clan bids for Hemedti’s ear, Burhan’s US visa troubles, Kordofan battles come to head as RSF presses ahead in Blue Nile, Kiir re-engineers electoral scene
content:

here

.




As world leaders gathered in New York this week for talks at the United Nations General Assembly, Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan had to watch the proceeding from afar. And that is because, while the military leader had been penciled in to give a speech to the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, the US denied his visa. 




For Sudanese officials familiar with the internal planning, the move doesn’t come as a complete surprise, given that the US had sanctioned Burhan last year and the relationship has become increasingly fractious. But the visa denial is yet another sign of the frustration and polarization that dominates talks over a humanitarian truce, ceasefire and political settlement to Sudan’s war. 




Sources in New York and others familiar with communications between Sudan, regional capitals and the US described efforts to mitigate the crisis, which they viewed as US pressure on Sudan to accept a 90-day humanitarian truce, while emphasizing that the government would not back down from its core position. 




But the military wasn’t the only one facing a political crisis this week. In Darfur, the Nawaiba, one of the Rizeigat’s main clans in East Darfur, announced it was withdrawing from the nazirate of Musa Madibo, the head of the Rizeigat.

author: Hassan Alnaser
title: After seizing Tigray airports, TPLF announces ‘defensive war’ against Ethiopian govt
content:
The confrontation between the Tigray regional government and the Ethiopian federal government entered a new phase on Wednesday when Tigrayan forces seized control of the 

Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports.

 




Clashes broke out at several locations in the restive northern state, the site of a two-year civil war that concluded in 2022, and in the neighboring 

Afar

 region — a development that has pushed the Ethiopian conflict back toward open warfare, four years after the signing of the 

Pretoria Agreement

 that ended the previous war between the 

Tigray People’s Liberation Front 

and federal forces.




A source in the Tigray regional administration told Mada Masr that the seizure of the airports was part of a military redeployment that began in the early hours of Wednesday, with Tigrayan forces 

using 

the airports as facilities of operational importance amid the expanding scope of the fighting.




In the wake of the TPLF takeover, Ethiopian Airlines 

announced

 the suspension of flights to the three airports due to the “current situation” in the Tigray region.

 




A Tigrayan military source noted that Wednesday’s developments followed months of troop buildup and limited skirmishes along the front lines, describing Wednesday’s events as a shift from a phase of mutual pressure to direct confrontation.

author: Mariam Soliman
title: Court upholds sentence against Omnia Sweidan for publishing description of obstetric violence at Al-Shatby Hospital
content:
Omnia Sweidan’s appeal against a fine and prison sentence she received for a Facebook post describing abuses against patients was rejected on Thursday, according to her lawyer Ahmed Ragheb. 




Sweidan was tried earlier this year on charges relating to the post which detailed obstetric and other forms of violence against women at Alexandria’s Al-Shatby Hospital. A misdemeanor court ultimately 

issued

 her with a six-month prison sentence and a LE20,000 fine. The prison sentence was issued with a three-year suspension. 




Ragheb told Mada Masr that after he attended her hearing at the Economic Misdemeanors Court at Dekheila Courthouse this week, the court rejected her appeal and upheld the 

July

 ruling.




Sweidan’s post described instances of physical and sexual abuse of women patients at Alexandria University’s Al-Shatby Hospital. Sweidan recounted incidents she said she had witnessed or heard discussed during her medical training in the hospital’s obstetrics and gynecology department six years earlier.




The post went viral within hours and drew tens of thousands of 

shares

 and comments amid a conversation that quickly turned to other instances of obstetric violence, with many 

women

 sharing their own experiences of mistreatment in maternity wards.

 

Healthcare professionals who spoke to Mada Masr 

said

 the abuses she recounted reflected a common and per
